messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT OPENED (HIGH) - runtime-prod 5xx spike detected. Alert: >10% 5xx over 1m across /v1/generate. Pager: eng-oncall, runtime-oncall.
Maya: saw the bot, i'm on it. starting triage, grabbing recent deploys and metrics.
Sam: thanks. quick question — if this looks like model runtime (OOM/kv-cache), should we page runtime-oncall or infra?
Maya: initial telemetry looks like elevated latency + 5xx from the runtime tier, not infra networking. but need logs to be sure.
Kai: infra-oncall here — if you see GPU allocation errors or node churn, page infra. If it's per-request kernel failures, page runtime.
Olivia: listing primary/secondary for the shift: primary = Maya, secondary = Sam. Coverage: Kai is on-call for infra, Linda for security, Support-SRE for customer comms.
Maya: copying runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-5xx (section: "initial triage checklist"). follow steps 1-3.
Sam: running the suggested log query now: ```
# k8s logs grep
kubectl -n runtime-prod logs -l app=runtime --since=2m | grep -E "ERROR|OOM|KVCache"
```
Maya: seeing repeated "KVCacheEvictionError" in logs + stack: ```
ERROR runtime.core: kv_cache.cpp:142 eviction failed: insufficient memory
backtrace: runtime::ServeRequest -> kv::evict -> mem::alloc
```
Maya: that smells like model-serving memory pressure / incorrect quantization slice. Paging runtime-oncall (pinging Sam). @Sam : are you able to look at model flags / recent hotpatches?
Sam: I'm on it. checking recent model variants and quant flags. I also see a small config push 12m ago that bumped max_seq from 2048->4096 for a canary. rolling that back for the canary now.
Kai: FYI infra metrics show no node autoscaler events and host level mem ok. not seeing network blips.
Linda: security-oncall checking — any signs of malformed requests or abuse patterns? I can run quick IP/rate filters.
Support-SRE: opening customer impact thread. So far 7 customer reports (chat + error 503). tagging product/sales if this persists.
Maya: mitigation plan: 1) rollback canary model flag (Sam) 2) scale up runtime-pool by +2 replicas for 10m 3) enable temporary KV cache backpressure (runbook cmd below).
Maya: backpressure command (runbook): ```
# enable prefix-only caching and reduce cache window
redwoodctl runtime set-cache-policy --policy prefix-only --window 30s --target runtime-prod
```
Sam: rolled back canary flag at 3109876561. watching for drop in 5xx.
Maya: increased pool at 3109876568 (kubectl scale ...).
Maya: enabled cache backpressure at 3109876575.
Olivia: recording timeline and who did what for postmortem. primary = Maya (lead triage), secondary = Sam (runtime), infra owner = Kai, security = Linda, support = Support-SRE.
Support-SRE: customer comms draft: "We're investigating increased errors on runtime-prod impacting generation endpoints. Engineers are mitigating; we'll update in 30 min." please sign-off if OK.
Linda: running quick abuse query: no anomalous source IPs. good to proceed.
Kai: infra clear, standing by.
Maya: 5xx rate down to ~1.6% at 3109876587. moving to monitoring. plan: keep extra replicas for 20m, then revert if stable.
Sam: tagging followups for post-incident: - investigate canary flag test coverage, - add metric for KVCacheEvictionError, - set alert threshold for sequence-length config pushes.
Olivia: note coverage gap: upcoming 02:00 UTC shift has no secondary assigned. I'll ping rotations to fill that hole.
Maya: agree, Olivia please update oncall rota. Also schedule a brief async runbook refresh to include the cache backpressure CLI snippet.
Support-SRE: will update customers in 25m with improved status.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> MEDIUM (mitigated), assigned to postmortem.
Maya: closing the live mitigation. leaving notes for postmortem. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
